Definition: Whether the system enables individuals to authenticate themselves or their documents digitally through electronic verification
Comments: The CNIB is a physical card with barcode and Teslin material — no chip, no RFID, no digital authentication capability. DPI Map records 'Enables authentication: NA'. The new CIB-AES will include an electronic chip storing biometric data to enable digital authentication, but mass production only started January 2026.

Definition: Whether authentication is possible through a centralized government portal or digital gateway
Comments: DPI Map records 'Enables authentication via government portal: NA'. No government digital portal using the CNIB for authentication exists. The World Bank e-Burkina project aimed to create e-services infrastructure but has not produced a functional government portal with ID-based authentication.

Definition: Whether individuals can view their data held in the ID database and see how it has been accessed
Comments: No self-service portal or mechanism for individuals to view or manage their personal data held in the ONI CNIB database. No evidence of any data subject access portal. Data rights exist under Law n°001-2021/AN but no digital mechanism to exercise them against the ID database.

Definition: Whether the system enables Know Your Customer (KYC) packet collection for service provision, particularly financial services
Comments: DPI Map records 'Enables KYC: NA'. No automated/digital KYC using the CNIB system. Banks use manual physical ID verification. UEMOA directive governs AML/KYC requirements using physical CNIB. Planned digital eKYC as part of WURI project not yet operational.

Definition: Whether the ID authority and system are subject to general oversight of the courts and judicial review
Value Name: Yes, but not specific to ID
Comments: Burkina Faso has general judicial oversight through the Administrative Supreme Court (Conseil d'État) which can hear appeals against CIL decisions. DPI Map notes 'Legally binding redress mechanism: NA'. No ID-specific judicial oversight mechanisms identified.

Definition: Whether the civil registration and digital ID systems are integrated
Comments: Integration between ONI (CNIB) and civil registry (DGMEC) is very limited. iCivil digital birth registration system launched in 2020 is partially operational (130 of 2,584 registration points). No formal linkage between CNIB issuance and civil registry. Plans exist to digitize civil registry and link to ID system.

Definition: Whether procedural rules for collection, storage, and sharing of ID-related personal data are publicly available and established
Comments: DPI Map records 'Terms of data storage and sharing available: NO' and 'Data handling terms exist: NO'. No publicly available data sharing rules for the ID system. Data leak disclosure process does not exist per DPI Map.

Definition: Whether specific regulation or policy addresses digital ID beyond general identification legislation
Comments: DPI Map records: No regulation specifically for digital ID. The legal and regulatory framework does not support digital technology for civil registration, which only considers paper-based registers as legal documents. No dedicated digital ID law.

Definition: Whether national data protection legislation exists and covers personal data linked to the ID system
Comments: Law n°010-2004/AN on the Protection of Personal Data was enacted in 2004 — one of Africa's earliest data protection laws. Updated by Law n°001-2021/AN (March 30, 2021). Establishes rights to consent, access, correction, erasure, and redress. Enforced by the CIL.

Definition: Whether a Data Protection Authority or similar body regulates ID data collection and sharing by the ID system
Comments: The Commission de l'Informatique et des Libertés (CIL) was established as the data protection authority. It is empowered to conduct inspections, impose fines (CFAF 500,000–5,000,000), and order imprisonment (6 months–5 years). It actively enforces data protection laws for personal data processing.

Definition: Whether the digital ID credential serves as legal proof of an individual's identity as codified in law
Comments: The CNIB serves as the primary legal identification document for Burkinabé citizens. Required for voting, banking, employment, SIM card purchase, and travel. DPI Map notes 'Claim digital ID: YES'. Established by Loi n°005-2001/AN as official proof of identity and nationality.

Definition: Whether formal legislation (act, law, regulation) governs digital identity including identification acts, digital ID laws, or equivalent legislation
Comments: The CNIB is established by Loi n°005-2001/AN; physical characteristics defined by Décret 2003-668. The Code des Personnes et de la Famille (1989) governs civil registration. A unique ID number decree (2013-1028) exists. Legal framework exists but does not fully support digital technology.

Definition: Whether the system and the production of credentials can be managed, maintained and developed by in-country technical staff (as opposed to foreign vendors)
Comments: ONI relies on remote assistance and training from the Canadian Bank Note Company for CNIB production. iCivil uses French company Prooftag for bubble tags. The new CIB-AES uses Chinese firm Emptech for biometric enrollment hardware/software. In-country staff (250 police/gendarmerie officers) manage day-to-day operations.

Definition: Whether the Ministry of Finance has oversight of the financing and development of the digital ID system
Comments: ONI is a semi-autonomous, self-funded authority under the Ministry of Security (previously Ministry of Territorial Administration). No evidence of direct Ministry of Finance oversight of the ID system. ONI funds operations primarily through CNIB fee revenues.

Definition: Whether the ongoing management, maintenance and development of the ID system can be funded by sustainable domestic resources
Comments: ONI is primarily self-funded through CNIB card fees (2,500 CFA per card; new CIB-AES at 3,500 CFA). However, major infrastructure investments depend on external support (World Bank WURI project ~US$75M IDA credit; UNFPA, IOM for iCivil). Mixed domestic-external financing model.

Definition: Whether the system collects biometric data and which modalities are collected (fingerprints, facial image, iris scans)
Comments: CNIB collects 2 flat fingerprints and facial recognition (digital photo). Facial biometrics added to the system in 2009 alongside fingerprint deduplication via AFIS. The new CIB-AES also includes fingerprints, signature, and digital photo captured electronically.

Definition: Whether the country has established or is actively developing a national digital identity system, including foundational ID systems that enable authentication across multiple services. Fully deployed means operational nationwide and accepting new registrations.
Comments: Burkina Faso has had the CNIB (Carte Nationale d'Identité Burkinabè) fully deployed nationwide since 2004 under the Office of National Identification (ONI), with 7.2M+ records and 73% of adults 15+ covered. A new AES biometric card (CIB-AES) entered mass production in January 2026.

Definition: Whether the digital ID system is designed to be interoperable across government agencies and with other systems through APIs or data exchange protocols
Comments: No formal interoperability between ONI/CNIB and civil registry (DGMEC), electoral commission, health, or tax systems. No shared unique ID across systems. No formal MOUs or protocols for interconnectivity. The iCivil system offers partial linkage to health facilities but is not yet integrated with ONI.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for opening bank accounts and accessing financial services
Comments: The CNIB is required for opening a bank account and accessing financial services in Burkina Faso. Per Tanager International (2023): 'Voting in elections, holding a job, opening a bank account — all require an identity card.' CNIB is accepted but ownership is not 100% mandatory for all financial transactions.

Definition: Whether credentials are issued free of charge
Comments: The CNIB costs 2,500 CFA francs (~USD 4). The new CIB-AES costs 3,500 CFA francs (~USD 6). Not free. The price increase reflects polycarbonate material and enhanced security features. Birth certificates cost ~1,000 CFA; late registration requires a costly suppletive judgment.

Definition: Whether the digital ID is recognized or interoperable across borders through regional agreements or travel documents
Value Name: Recognized in some regional contexts (e.g., ECOWAS travel)
Comments: The CIB-AES biometric ID card is designed for cross-border recognition within the Alliance of Sahel States (AES: Burkina Faso, Mali, Niger). Launched December 2025, with a 5-year transition period. The card includes AES logos and is recognized across the three member states. Not yet formally interoperable with ECOWAS.

Definition: Age in years at which an individual becomes eligible to register for digital ID
Comments: The new CIB-AES biometric card is available from age 5 (mandatory from age 13) per November 2025 decree and January 2026 mass production launch. The previous CNIB was mandatory from age 15. The new system significantly lowers the eligibility age to 5 years.

Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government digital identity systems and credentials. 30 variables in 5 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Whether registration for digital ID is mandatory, optional, or mandatory for specific groups
Comments: CNIB was mandatory for all citizens aged 15+. The new CIB-AES is mandatory from age 13. Enrollment for younger children (ages 5-12) is optional. Previous CNIB mandatory from age 15. Mandatory for subset of the population (those 13+).

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for accessing public healthcare services
Comments: National ID accepted for health services but not universally mandatory. Burkina Faso has a free healthcare policy for children under 5 and pregnant women that does not require ID. CNIB required for formal health insurance enrollment. Healthcare can be accessed without an ID card at primary facilities.

Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government digital identity systems and credentials. 30 variables in 5 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Whether non-nationals including refugees, asylum seekers, and permanent residents are eligible to register
Comments: The CNIB is issued exclusively to Burkinabé citizens. Non-nationals (foreigners, refugees, stateless persons) are not eligible for the national ID card. The WURI project plans to eventually make the foundational ID system inclusive of all persons in the territory regardless of nationality.

Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government digital identity systems and credentials. 30 variables in 5 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Percentage of eligible population that has been issued or registered with digital ID credentials
Comments: 73% of the population aged 15 and over held a CNIB biometric identity card (facial recognition) as of 2016 per World Bank ID4D diagnostic. Total population coverage is lower given large under-15 population. New CIB-AES from age 5 expected to expand coverage from January 2026.

Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government digital identity systems and credentials. 30 variables in 5 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Whether ID system undergoes regular security audits, penetration testing, or vulnerability assessments
Comments: No evidence of independent security audits or published security reviews of the ONI/CNIB system. DPI Map notes 'Data leak disclosure process exists: NO'. ONI employs police/gendarmerie staff and uses deduplication (AFIS) but no formal external security certification or published audit found.

Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government digital identity systems and credentials. 30 variables in 5 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for registering for social assistance programs and accessing social services
Comments: The CNIB is used for access to social services including social safety nets and school registration. However, some social safety net programs (e.g., for extreme poor) do not require documentation. The Social Registry (RSU) expansion aims to use ID linkage but not universally mandatory.
